Rashi on Sotah 32a:10:1.english: Which are in Samaria - Near Samaria.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:11:1.english: At the bottom in the middle - Between the two mountains.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:11:2.english: On this side and on that side - On the mountains.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:12:1.hebrew: הפכו - הלוים פניהם כלפי הר גריזים ופתחו בברכה. כל הארורים היו אומרים תחלה בלשון ברכה:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:12:1.english: They turned - the Levites [turned] their faces toward Mount Gerizim and opened with a blessing. All the curses they would say first in the language of a blessing.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:12:2.hebrew: אלו ואלו - שבהר גריזים ושבהר עיבל. והא דכתיב ״ואלה יעמדו לברך״, לא שהיו השבטים מברכין ומקללין, אלא הלוים העומדים בין שני ההרים הופכין פניהם להר גריזים בברכה ולהר עיבל בקללה:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:12:2.english: These and those - [Those] who were on Mount Gerizim and [those] who were on Mount Ebal. And [as for] that which is written, "These shall stand to bless," [it does] not [mean] that the tribes were blessing and cursing; rather, the Levites, who were standing between the two mountains, would turn their faces toward Mount Gerizim for the blessing and toward Mount Ebal for the curse.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:13:1.hebrew: הביאו את האבנים - כדכתיב: "ובנית שם מזבח" וגו', "וכתבת עליהן את כל דברי התורה הזאת באר היטב":
Rashi on Sotah 32a:13:1.english: They brought the stones - As it is written: "And there you shall build an altar," etc., "And you shall write upon them all the words of this Torah, clearly elucidated."

Rashi on Sotah 32a:13:2.hebrew: ונטלו את האבנים - סתרו את המזבח לאחר שהעלו העולות והשלמים, כדכתיב: ״והעלית עליו עולות״ (שם כז):
Rashi on Sotah 32a:13:2.english: And they took the stones - They dismantled the altar after they had offered the burnt-offerings and the peace-offerings, as it is written: "And you shall offer burnt-offerings upon it" (ibid., 27[:6]).

Rashi on Sotah 32a:1:1.hebrew: והכא במאי עסקינן - דקתני: "עד אחד אומר נטמאת, ושנים אומרים לא נטמאת — היתה שותה", ואוקימנא בפסולי עדות, ובין בבת אחת בין בזה אחר זה, כר' נחמיה. ועל כרחיך, דבזה אחר זה איצטריך עיקר לאשמועינן, דאי בבת אחת — מאי "הלך אחר רוב דיעות" איכא? בחד וחד נמי היתה שותה! [אלא] בהכי עסקינן, דההוא דאתא מעיקרא ואמר "נטמאת", אשה הויא; הילכך, אפי' בזה אחר זה אתו תרתי ומבטלי לה:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:1:1.english: And with what are we dealing here - Where [the Mishnah] teaches: "One witness says 'she was defiled' and two say 'she was not defiled,' she would drink," and we established [the Mishnah] as referring to disqualified witnesses, whether simultaneously or one after another, in accordance with Rabbi Nechemiah. And perforce, it was primarily necessary to teach us [the case of] one after another; for if [it were only] simultaneously, what "follow the majority of opinions" is there? Even with one [witness] and one [witness], she would drink! [Rather,] we are dealing with a case where the one who came initially and said "she was defiled" was a woman; therefore, even one after another, two [women] come and nullify her [testimony].

Rashi on Sotah 32a:2:1.hebrew: ותרצה לדרבי נחמיה הכי כו' - דהא דאמרן לעיל, ועשו שתי נשים באיש אחד כו', לאו סיפא דמילתיה דרבי נחמיה הוא, אלא פירושא דמילתיה הוא, דאנו פרשין לה הכי:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:2:1.english: And amend [the statement] of Rabbi Nechemyah like this, etc. - For that which we said above, "And they made two women against one man, etc.," is not the end of Rabbi Nechemyah's statement; rather, it is an explanation of his statement, as we explain it thus.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:2:2.hebrew: כי פלגא ופלגא דמי - כלומר, כי חד וחד; ואי בבת אחת אתו, אוקי תרי לבהדי חד ואוקמיה אספיקא. ואי בזה אחר זה, וההוא דהאמינה תורה קדם ואתא ברישא, הוה ליה כשנים והנך כחד, ואין דבריהם במקומו. והיכא דשתים אומרות "נטמאת" ועד אחד כשר אומר "לא נטמאת", היתה שותה, דכי חד וחד נינהו. ומתניתין דקתני "לא היתה שותה", כגון דההוא חד הוה פסול:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:2:2.english: It is like half and half - That is to say, like one [against] one; and if they come simultaneously, place the two [women] against the one [man] and leave [the matter] in doubt. And if [they come] one after another, and that [witness] whom the Torah believed preceded and came first, he is like two [witnesses] and those [two women] are like one [witness], and their words have no [standing] in his place. And where two [women] say, "She became defiled," and one valid witness says, "She did not become defiled," she would drink [the bitter waters], for they are like one [against] one. And [as for] our Mishnah, which teaches, "She would not drink," [that is] a case where that one [witness] was disqualified.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:3:1.english: And why do I [need] two [cases] regarding those disqualified from [bearing] witness - [For] the Mishnah to teach, "Follow the majority of opinions."

Rashi on Sotah 32a:3:2.english: To be stringent - that she should drink [the bitter water].

Rashi on Sotah 32a:3:3.english: To be lenient - To be lenient upon her, so that she does not drink.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:3:4.hebrew: לא אזלינן - בתר רוב דיעות בפסולי עדות. והיכא דשתים אומרות נטמאת ואחד אומר לא נטמאת, כיון דאיכא הכחשה כל דהו, נימא אוקי האי לבהדי הנך ואוקי מילתא אספיקא ותשתה, קא משמע לן:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:3:4.english: We do not follow - the majority of opinions among those disqualified from bearing witness. And where two [women] say, "She was defiled," and one says, "She was not defiled," since there is any contradiction whatsoever, we would say: place this one against those, and leave the matter in a state of doubt and she should drink [the bitter water]; [therefore, the Mishnah] teaches us [that we do follow the majority].

Rashi on Sotah 32a:5:1.english: These are recited - We have the reading: "(in any language)."

Rashi on Sotah 32a:5:2.hebrew: פרשת סוטה - מה שהכהן אומר לה, ולא אמרי' צריך לאומרה בלשון הקודש כדרך שנכתב. ובספרי אמרי', דאי לא כתיב קרא להתיר בכל לשון כדלקמן, ה"א ניגמר מיבמה בקל וחומר, ומה יבמה קלה לא עשה בה כל הלשונות כלשון הקודש, סוטה חמורה לא כל שכן:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:5:2.english: The portion of a sotah - [That is,] what the priest says to her, and we do not say [that] one must recite it in the Holy Tongue in the manner in which it is written. And in the Sifri we say that if a verse were not written to permit [reciting it] in any language, as [will be explained] below, I would have said [that] we should derive [it] from a yevamah by means of a kal vachomer [a fortiori inference]: Just as [in the case of] a yevamah, which is lenient, [Scripture] did not make all languages like the Holy Tongue in her [case], [so too in the case of] a sotah, which is stringent, is it not all the more so?

Rashi on Sotah 32a:5:3.hebrew: ווידוי מעשר - בשנה השלישית, "בערתי הקודש מן הבית" (דברים כו) — שהוא מוציא כל מעשרותיו ומבערן מביתו, ואין יכול עוד להשהותם, ונותן מעשר ראשון ללוי, ומעשר עני לעניים, ומעשר שני של שתי שנים שעברו מעליהו לירושלים עכשיו, אם לא העלהו. ומתוודה: "בערתי הקדש" — זה מעשר שני; "וגם נתתיו ללוי" — זה מעשר ראשון; "לגר ליתום ולאלמנה" — זה מעשר עני. ואומרו בכל לשון, כדיליף לקמן, ולא אמרינן בלשון זה הזקיקו הכתוב לאומרה בלה"ק:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:5:3.english: And the confession of tithes - In the third year, "I have removed the sacred [portion] from the house" (Deuteronomy 26[:13]) — for he removes all his tithes and clears them out of his house, and may no longer delay them; and he gives the first tithe to the Levite, and the poor man's tithe to the poor, and the second tithe of the two previous years he brings up to Jerusalem now, if he has not [already] brought it up. And he confesses: "I have removed the sacred [portion]" — this is the second tithe; "and I have also given it to the Levite" — this is the first tithe; "to the stranger, to the orphan, and to the widow" — this is the poor man's tithe. And he recites it in any language, as [the Gemara] derives below, and we do not say that Scripture required him to recite it in this language, [namely] in the Holy Tongue.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:5:4.hebrew: ושבועת העדות ושבועת הפקדון - בכל לשון שהשביעוהו וכפר ולא הודה, חייב קרבן עולה ויורד האמור בשבועת העדות, ואשם גזילות בשבועת הפקדון:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:5:4.english: And the oath of testimony and the oath on a deposit - In whatever language they adjured him, and he denied [it] and did not admit [to it], he is liable [to bring] the sliding-scale offering stated regarding the oath of testimony, and a guilt-offering for robbery regarding the oath on a deposit.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:1.hebrew: ואלו נאמרין בלה"ק - ולא אמרינן נגמר מהנך דלעיל, שנכתב ונסדר עליהן כל מצות דיבורם, ואין צריך לאומרן בלה"ק כדכתיב בכולהו, משום דבהני כתיב עיכובא:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:1.english: And these are recited in the sacred tongue - And we do not say: Let us derive [these] from those [listed] above, regarding which the entire mitzvah of their speaking was written and arranged [in the Torah], and [yet] there is no need to recite them in the sacred tongue as is written regarding all of them — because regarding these, an essential requirement is written.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:2.english: The recitation of first fruits - That he would recite from "An Aramean sought to destroy my father" [Deut. 26:5] until the end of the entire section.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:3.hebrew: וחליצת יבמה - היא אומרת "מאן יבמי וגו'", והוא אומר "לא חפצתי לקחתה", ואחר החליצה היא אומרת "ככה יעשה לאיש וגו'":
Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:3.english: And ḥalitza of a yevama - She says, "My husband's brother refuses, etc.," and he says, "I do not wish to take her," and after the ḥalitza she says, "Thus shall be done to the man, etc."

Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:4.hebrew: ברכות וקללות - שאמרן יהושע וישראל בהר גריזים והר עיבל:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:4.english: Blessings and curses - Which Joshua and Israel recited on Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:5.english: The Priestly Benediction - Raising of the hands.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:6.hebrew: ברכת כהן גדול - ביום הכפורים, אחר עבודת היום שלפני ולפנים, היה קורא בתורה את הפרשה ומברך שמנה ברכות, כדמפרש במתניתין:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:6.english: The blessing of the High Priest - On the Day of Atonement, after the service of the day in the innermost [sanctum], he would read the portion in the Torah and recite eight blessings, as it explains in the Mishnah.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:7.hebrew: ופרשת המלך - מפרש בסוף פירקא, והיא פרשת הקהל:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:7.english: And the portion of the king - [It] is explained at the end of the chapter, and it is the portion of Hakhel [the assembly].

Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:8.hebrew: ופרשת עגלה ערופה - ידינו לא שפכו וגו', כפר לעמך ישראל וגו' (דברים כא):
Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:8.english: And the portion of a heifer whose neck is broken - "Our hands did not shed, etc."; "Atone for Your people Israel, etc." (Deuteronomy 21).

Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:9.hebrew: פרשת משוח מלחמה - (שם כ) והיה כקרבכם אל וגו', שמע ישראל אתם קרבים היום וגו', כי ה' אלהיכם וגו:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:6:9.english: The portion of [the priest] anointed for war - (ibid. 20): "And it shall be, when you draw near to [the battle], etc."; "Hear, O Israel, you draw near this day, etc."; "For the Lord your God, etc."

Rashi on Sotah 32a:7:2.hebrew: ולהלן הוא אומר - בברכות וקללות של הר גריזים, ולקמן מפרש התם גופיה מנא לן:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:7:2.english: And below it states - In the blessings and curses of Mount Gerizim; and later [the Gemara] explains from where [we derive] that [passage] itself.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:9:1.hebrew: אינו צריך - ללמדה בגזרה שוה, שמעצמה היא למידה:
Rashi on Sotah 32a:9:1.english: It is not necessary - to derive it through a gezeira shava [verbal analogy], as it is learned from [the verse] itself.

Rashi on Sotah 32a:9:2.english: And she shall answer and say, “So” - Which implies: in this language she shall say [it].

Tosafot on Sotah 32a:3:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא כי אזלינן בתר רוב דיעות לחומרא אבל לקולא לא קמ"ל - ואם תאמר, הא ממתני' בפרק האשה שהלכה (יבמות ד' קיז:) וממתני' דפרק עגלה ערופה (לקמן סוטה דף מז.) שמעינן לה? י"ל, דהכא איצטריך דאפילו לקולא, אע"ג דרגלים לדבר. ועוד, דלא תנא פסולי העדות בהדיא במתני', להכי תנא גבי כל חד וחד:
Tosafot on Sotah 32a:3:1.english: "Lest you say that when we follow the majority opinion [it is] to be stringent, but to be lenient [we do] not [follow it], [therefore] it teaches us" - And if you ask: Do we not learn this from the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] HaIshah SheHalkhah (Yevamot 117b) and from the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Eglah Arufah (below, Sotah 47a)? One can answer that here it was necessary [to teach] that [we follow the majority] even to be lenient, even though there are grounds for the matter [i.e., circumstantial evidence]. And furthermore, because [the Mishnah] did not state "disqualified witnesses" explicitly in the Mishnah, therefore it taught [this law] regarding each and every one [of the cases].

Tosafot on Sotah 32a:5:1.hebrew: אלו נאמרין בלשונם [ה"ג בסדר הנשנה] - ופירוש: כל אדם בלשונו שהוא שומע, לאפוקי למדי שאינו אומר בלשון פרסי אם אינו שומעו; אבל "בכל לשון" משמע בין שומע בין אינו שומע, ובגמרא לא משמע הכי:
Tosafot on Sotah 32a:5:1.english: "These are recited in their language" [thus is the reading in the order of the Mishnah] - And the explanation [is]: every person in his own language that he understands, to the exclusion of a Mede, who does not recite [it] in the Persian language if he does not understand it; whereas "in any language" implies whether he understands [it] or does not understand [it], and in the Gemara it does not imply thus.

Tosafot on Sotah 32a:5:2.hebrew: קרית שמע ותפלה - תימה, אמאי שייר הלל וקידוש של שבת וברכת הפירות וברכת המצות? וליכא למימר דלא נקט אלא דאורייתא, דהא בפרק מי שמתו (ברכות דף כא.) משמע דתפלה וקרית שמע דרבנן, ועוד דהתם (דף כ:) משמע דקידוש דאורייתא, והכי משמע נמי בריש מסכת נזיר (דף ג:). בשלמא מקרא מגילה איכא למימר להכי שייר, דתנא בפ"ב דמגילה (דף יז.): "הלועז ששמע אשורית יצא"; אלא הני אמאי שייר? ונראה דהני נאמרים בכל לשון אפי' אינו שומע, הלכך לא דמו להני דמתני' דנאמרין דוקא בלשונם:
Tosafot on Sotah 32a:5:2.english: Keriyat Shema and Prayer - It is puzzling: why did [the Tanna] omit Hallel, Kiddush of Shabbat, blessings over fruits, and blessings over commandments? And one cannot say that he only mentioned biblical [obligations], for in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shemeto (Berakhot 21a) it is implied that Prayer and Keriyat Shema are rabbinic, and furthermore, there (20b) it is implied that Kiddush is biblical, and so too is it implied at the beginning of tractate Nazir (3b). Granted, [as for] the reading of the Megillah, one can say that for this reason he omitted [it], for it was taught in the second chapter of Megillah (17a): "A non-Hebrew speaker who heard [it in] Ashurit [i.e., Hebrew] has fulfilled [his obligation]"; but why did he omit these? And it appears that these [omitted items] may be recited in any language even if one does not understand [it]; therefore they are not similar to those of our Mishnah, which are recited specifically in their [understood] language.
